followUps.scope: GP braking and dry/wet two-lap contact races
followUps.result: Braking suite and all three contact-race cases pass after finite lever response and wet-contact steering correction. Mixed-class pace and overtaking remain open.

followUps.scope: Motocross telemetry candidate, all motocross unit files
followUps.result: Three original wheel-pickup tests repaired; all remaining failures also reproduce in the broader baseline. No assertion thresholds changed.

followUps.scope: Passive deep-contact response and touchdown compatibility
followUps.result: Hard-stop contact exchanges horizontal/heave/pitch momentum instead of adding heave at prescribed forward speed. 270 analytic contact combinations prove non-increasing kinetic energy and removal only of closing velocity. Original launch height, crash and riding checks pass unchanged. AI/supermoto no longer arm the obsolete pickup flag for one touchdown frame.

followUps.scope: Motocross final focused suite after contact fixes and contract review
followUps.result: Four terrain/tyre contact tests remain failing. Recovery distance now accumulates signed lap-wrapped travel and also rejects station jumps. Three brake assertions now test finite wheel response within 16.7 ms, preserve original force differences and add immediate rotor/unsupported-contact checks; fork movement remains below 1 mm. The finite-brush settling assertion verifies actual slip telemetry, <0.1% mismatch and coarse/fine agreement rather than forcing an ideal zero-slip constraint. These contract corrections are not counted as new physical behavior improvements.

A one-metre target-tracking reserve applies only while GP corridors are narrowed. Swept collision, longitudinal braking and full-width/mixed-class rules remain unchanged. Real catch-and-pass/replay, GP braking approach and shared traffic: 28/28 pass. Wider candidate run: 55/56 pass, with the same pre-existing mixed GP/superbike pace failure (83.57565 vs 83.12327 s); all dry/wet GP contact races pass.
